questions.stem: What is the probability of getting a head when a fair coin is tossed once?
questions.keySolution:
When a fair coin is tossed, there are \(2\) equally likely outcomes: Head (H) and Tail (T).
Probability of getting a head = \(\frac{\text{Number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{Total number of outcomes}} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: Two fair coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting exactly one head?
What is the probability of getting at least one head when two fair coins are tossed?
Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes when three coins are tossed = \(2^3 = 8\)
Favorable outcomes for exactly two heads: {HHT, HTH, THH}
Number of favorable outcomes = \(3\)
Probability = \(\frac{3}{8}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of getting all tails when four fair coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes when four coins are tossed = \(2^4 = 16\)
Favorable outcome for all tails: {TTTT}
Number of favorable outcomes = \(1\)
Probability = \(\frac{1}{16}\)

questions.stem: Five fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least four heads?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^5 = 32\)
At least four heads means exactly four heads OR exactly five heads
Ways to get exactly four heads = \(\binom{5}{4} = 5\)
Ways to get exactly five heads = \(\binom{5}{5} = 1\)
Total favorable outcomes = \(5 + 1 = 6\)
Probability = \(\frac{6}{32} = \frac{3}{16}\)

questions.stem: A coin is tossed three times. What is the probability that the first toss is a head given that at least one head appears?
questions.keySolution:
Let A = first toss is head, B = at least one head appears
Sample space: {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT}
Event B: {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH} - \(7\) outcomes
Event A∩B: {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT} - \(4\) outcomes
P(A|B) = \(\frac{P(A ∩ B)}{P(B)} = \frac{4/8}{7/8} = \frac{4}{7}\)

questions.stem: Two coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at most one head?
What is the probability of getting exactly \(3\) heads when \(5\) fair coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^5 = 32\)
Number of ways to get exactly \(3\) heads from \(5\) coins = \(\binom{5}{3} = \frac{5!}{3!2!} = 10\)
Probability = \(\frac{10}{32} = \frac{5}{16}\)

questions.stem: Four coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting exactly one tail?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^4 = 16\)
Exactly one tail means exactly three heads
Number of ways = \(\binom{4}{1} = 4\) (or \(\binom{4}{3} = 4\))
Probability = \(\frac{4}{16} = \frac{1}{4}\)

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed \(4\) times. What is the probability that heads and tails appear alternately?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^4 = 16\)
Alternating patterns: HTHТ and THTH
Number of favorable outcomes = \(2\)
Probability = \(\frac{2}{16} = \frac{1}{8}\)

questions.stem: Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at most two heads?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^3 = 8\)
At most two heads means not getting three heads
P(at most two heads) = \(1 - P(\text{three heads}) = 1 - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of getting an odd number of heads when three fair coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
Sample space: {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT}
Odd number of heads: \(1\) head or \(3\) heads
Outcomes with \(1\) head: {HTT, THT, TTH} - \(3\) outcomes
Outcomes with \(3\) heads: {HHH} - \(1\) outcome
Total favorable outcomes = \(3 + 1 = 4\)
Probability = \(\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that both coins show the same face?
Five fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^5 = 32\)
Number of ways to choose \(2\) positions for heads out of \(5\) = \(\binom{5}{2} = \frac{5!}{2!3!} = 10\)
Probability = \(\frac{10}{32} = \frac{5}{16}\)

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed until a head appears. What is the probability that exactly \(3\) tosses are needed?
questions.keySolution:
For exactly \(3\) tosses to be needed, the sequence must be TTH
P(T) = \(\frac{1}{2}\), P(H) = \(\frac{1}{2}\)
P(TTH) = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{8}\)

questions.stem: Four coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least \(2\) heads?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^4 = 16\)
At least \(2\) heads = \(1 - P(0 \text{ heads}) - P(1 \text{ head})\)
P(0 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{0}}{16} = \frac{1}{16}\)
P(1 head) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{1}}{16} = \frac{4}{16}\)
P(at least 2 heads) = \(1 - \frac{1}{16} - \frac{4}{16} = \frac{11}{16}\)

questions.stem: Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that at least two consecutive coins show heads?
questions.keySolution:
Sample space: {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT}
Outcomes without consecutive heads: {HTH, HTT, THT, TTH} = \(4\) outcomes
Outcomes with at least two consecutive heads = \(8-4 = 4\)
Probability = \(\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of getting exactly one head in the first three tosses when a fair coin is tossed five times?
questions.keySolution:
We need exactly one head in the first three tosses
The last two tosses can be anything
Probability of exactly one head in first three tosses = \(\binom{3}{1} \times (\frac{1}{2})^3 = 3 \times \frac{1}{8} = \frac{3}{8}\)
The last two tosses don't affect this probability

questions.stem: Two fair coins are tossed \(3\) times. What is the probability of getting at least one head in each toss?
questions.keySolution:
P(at least one head when two coins are tossed) = \(1 - P(\text{both tails}) = 1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\)
For this to happen in each of the \(3\) tosses:
P(at least one head in each toss) = \((\frac{3}{4})^3 = \frac{27}{64}\)

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed \(4\) times. What is the probability that the number of heads is even?
questions.keySolution:
Even number of heads: \(0, 2, 4\) heads
P(0 heads) = \(\binom{4}{0}(\frac{1}{2})^4 = 1 \times \frac{1}{16} = \frac{1}{16}\)
P(2 heads) = \(\binom{4}{2}(\frac{1}{2})^4 = 6 \times \frac{1}{16} = \frac{6}{16}\)
P(4 heads) = \(\binom{4}{4}(\frac{1}{2})^4 = 1 \times \frac{1}{16} = \frac{1}{16}\)
Total = \(\frac{1+6+1}{16} = \frac{8}{16} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of getting more heads than tails when \(5\) fair coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
More heads than tails means at least \(3\) heads (since we have \(5\) coins)
P(3 heads) = \(\binom{5}{3}(\frac{1}{2})^5 = 10 \times \frac{1}{32} = \frac{10}{32}\)
P(4 heads) = \(\binom{5}{4}(\frac{1}{2})^5 = 5 \times \frac{1}{32} = \frac{5}{32}\)
P(5 heads) = \(\binom{5}{5}(\frac{1}{2})^5 = 1 \times \frac{1}{32} = \frac{1}{32}\)
Total = \(\frac{10+5+1}{32} = \frac{16}{32} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability that the first coin shows head given that exactly two heads appear?
Four fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting the same number of heads and tails?
questions.keySolution:
Same number of heads and tails means \(2\) heads and \(2\) tails
Total outcomes = \(2^4 = 16\)
Number of ways to get exactly \(2\) heads = \(\binom{4}{2} = 6\)
Probability = \(\frac{6}{16} = \frac{3}{8}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that when \(5\) coins are tossed, the first \(3\) coins show heads?
questions.keySolution:
The first \(3\) coins must show heads, the last \(2\) can show anything
P(first three are heads) = \((\frac{1}{2})^3 = \frac{1}{8}\)
The last two coins don't affect this probability

questions.stem: Two fair coins are tossed twice. What is the probability of getting at least one head in each pair of tosses?
questions.keySolution:
P(at least one head when two coins are tossed) = \(\frac{3}{4}\)
For this to happen in both pairs of tosses:
P(at least one head in each pair) = \((\frac{3}{4})^2 = \frac{9}{16}\)

questions.stem: A coin is tossed \(3\) times. What is the probability that heads appears for the first time on the third toss?
questions.keySolution:
For heads to appear for the first time on the third toss, the sequence must be TTH
P(TTH) = P(T) × P(T) × P(H) = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{8}\)

questions.stem: Five fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that at least one tail appears?
questions.keySolution:
P(at least one tail) = \(1 - P(\text{no tails}) = 1 - P(\text{all heads})\)
P(all heads) = \((\frac{1}{2})^5 = \frac{1}{32}\)
P(at least one tail) = \(1 - \frac{1}{32} = \frac{31}{32}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of getting exactly \(2\) heads when \(4\) fair coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^4 = 16\)
Number of ways to choose \(2\) positions for heads out of \(4\) = \(\binom{4}{2} = \frac{4!}{2!2!} = 6\)
Probability = \(\frac{6}{16} = \frac{3}{8}\)

questions.stem: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability that no two consecutive coins show the same face?
A fair coin is tossed \(5\) times. What is the probability that tails appears exactly twice?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^5 = 32\)
Exactly \(2\) tails means exactly \(3\) heads
Number of ways = \(\binom{5}{2} = \frac{5!}{2!3!} = 10\)
Probability = \(\frac{10}{32} = \frac{5}{16}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of getting at least \(3\) heads when \(4\) fair coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^4 = 16\)
At least \(3\) heads means exactly \(3\) heads OR exactly \(4\) heads
P(exactly 3 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{3}}{16} = \frac{4}{16}\)
P(exactly 4 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{4}}{16} = \frac{1}{16}\)
P(at least 3 heads) = \(\frac{4+1}{16} = \frac{5}{16}\)

questions.stem: A coin is biased such that P(Head) = \(\frac{1}{3}\). If the coin is tossed twice, what is the probability of getting exactly one head?
questions.keySolution:
P(Head) = \(\frac{1}{3}\), P(Tail) = \(1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\)
Exactly one head can occur as: HT or TH
P(HT) = \(\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{2}{9}\)
P(TH) = \(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{9}\)
P(exactly one head) = \(\frac{2}{9} + \frac{2}{9} = \frac{4}{9}\)

questions.stem: Three fair coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting more than one head?
questions.keySolution:
More than one head means \(2\) heads or \(3\) heads
P(exactly 2 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{3}{2}}{8} = \frac{3}{8}\)
P(exactly 3 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{3}{3}}{8} = \frac{1}{8}\)
P(more than one head) = \(\frac{3}{8} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: Four coins are tossed. What is the probability that at least \(3\) coins show the same face?
questions.keySolution:
At least \(3\) same means: exactly \(3\) heads + exactly \(3\) tails + all \(4\) heads + all \(4\) tails
P(exactly 3 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{3}}{16} = \frac{4}{16}\)
P(exactly 3 tails) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{1}}{16} = \frac{4}{16}\)
P(all 4 heads) = \(\frac{1}{16}\)
P(all 4 tails) = \(\frac{1}{16}\)
Total = \(\frac{4+4+1+1}{16} = \frac{10}{16} = \frac{5}{8}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that when \(5\) fair coins are tossed, the number of heads is greater than the number of tails by exactly \(1\)?
questions.keySolution:
Let H = number of heads, T = number of tails
We need H - T = 1 and H + T = 5
Solving: H = 3, T = 2
So we need exactly \(3\) heads
P(exactly 3 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{5}{3}}{2^5} = \frac{10}{32} = \frac{5}{16}\)

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed \(n\) times. If the probability of getting at least one head is \(\frac{7}{8}\), find \(n\).
Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that the third coin shows head given that at least two heads appear?
What is the probability of getting at least \(2\) tails when \(4\) coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
At least \(2\) tails = \(1 - P(0 \text{ tails}) - P(1 \text{ tail})\)
P(0 tails) = P(4 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{0}}{16} = \frac{1}{16}\)
P(1 tail) = P(3 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{4}{1}}{16} = \frac{4}{16}\)
P(at least 2 tails) = \(1 - \frac{1}{16} - \frac{4}{16} = 1 - \frac{5}{16} = \frac{11}{16}\)

questions.stem: Five coins are tossed. What is the probability that the number of heads and tails differ by at most \(1\)?
questions.keySolution:
We need |H - T| ≤ 1 where H + T = 5
Case 1: H - T = 1, so H = 3, T = 2
Case 2: H - T = -1, so H = 2, T = 3
P(exactly 3 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{5}{3}}{32} = \frac{10}{32}\)
P(exactly 2 heads) = \(\frac{\binom{5}{2}}{32} = \frac{10}{32}\)
Total probability = \(\frac{10}{32} + \frac{10}{32} = \frac{20}{32} = \frac{5}{8}\)

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed repeatedly until two consecutive heads appear. What is the probability that exactly \(4\) tosses are needed?
questions.keySolution:
For exactly 4 tosses, valid sequences: TTHH, HTHH
P(TTHH) = \((\frac{1}{2})^4 = \frac{1}{16}\)
P(HTHH) = \((\frac{1}{2})^4 = \frac{1}{16}\)
Total probability = \(\frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{2}{16} = \frac{1}{8}\)

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed \(3\) times. What is the probability that the number of heads in the first two tosses equals the number of heads in all three tosses?
questions.keySolution:
For the number of heads in first two tosses to equal total heads in all three tosses, the third toss must be a tail
P(third toss is tail) = \(\frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: Four fair coins are tossed. Find the probability that exactly two coins show heads and these two heads are on adjacent coins.
questions.keySolution:
Adjacent pairs possible: positions (1,2), (2,3), (3,4)
For each pair, pattern is HH in those positions, TT in other positions
Number of favorable outcomes = 3
Total outcomes = \(2^4 = 16\)
Probability = \(\frac{3}{16}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of getting exactly \(4\) heads when \(5\) fair coins are tossed?
questions.keySolution:
Total outcomes = \(2^5 = 32\)
Number of ways to choose 4 positions for heads out of 5 = \(\binom{5}{4} = 5\)
Probability = \(\frac{5}{32}\)
